title: IF...ELSE - Binary Decisions
description: Use ELSE to handle the opposite condition when IF is FALSE.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, what if the condition is FALSE? We need a backup plan. ELSE handles the 'otherwise' scenario."
story.context: ELSE provides an alternative code path when the IF condition is FALSE. It's the 'Plan B' of your test logic.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! IF handles one path, ELSE handles the other. Now your test covers both scenarios!"

instructions: Inside ELSE, log: 'Battery low - charging required'
Add END to close IF...ELSE block
Note: ELSE catches all cases where IF condition is FALSE
hints: ELSE is at same indentation level as IF

*** Test Cases ***
Battery Status

    IF    ${battery} >= 50

    ELSE

theory.title: Exercise 2.3.2: IF...ELSE
theory.content:
🔀 Two Paths, One Choice

MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, IF is one path. But what about the OTHER path? ELSE is your fallback when the condition fails."

"IF battery is full → do nothing. ELSE → charge batteries. One of these ALWAYS runs. No gaps, no uncertainty."

↔️ What is IF...ELSE?

ELSE - Alternative execution path when IF condition is FALSE

  • ✅ Binary decision - Two mutually exclusive paths
  • ✅ Guaranteed execution - One path ALWAYS runs
  • ✅ Complete coverage - Handle both TRUE and FALSE
  • ✅ Fallback logic - Default action when condition fails

Execution Flow:

  • 🔹 IF condition is TRUE → Run IF block, skip ELSE
  • 🔹 IF condition is FALSE → Skip IF block, run ELSE

📝 IF...ELSE Syntax

*** Test Cases ***
Temperature Control
    ${temp}=    Set Variable    65
    IF    ${temp} > 70
        Log    Temperature high - cooling
    ELSE
        Log    Temperature normal
    END

Execution (${temp} = 65):

  1. 🔹 Check: Is 65 > 70? → FALSE
  2. 🔹 Skip IF block
  3. 🔹 Run ELSE block: "Temperature normal"
  4. 🔹 END closes structure

📋 IF...ELSE Rules

  • 🔹 Position: ELSE at same level as IF
  • 🔹 Indentation: ELSE block indented like IF block
  • 🔹 Closing: One END for entire IF...ELSE
  • 🔹 Exclusivity: Only IF or ELSE runs, never both
  • 🔹 Optional: ELSE is optional, IF alone is valid

🎯 Your Task

Check battery level. IF >= 50 → healthy. ELSE → needs charging. Binary decision with complete coverage!
